culture-cycles.note: Holidays treated like Sundays under the cantonal rest-day laws (SECO table). The 1 August national day is the only federal holiday. Holidays on a Sunday are not moved.

laws.rule: Thurgau's rest-day law (Ruhetagsgesetz, §§ 1, 2, 4 to 6), in force from 1 January 2026: public rest days are Sundays; New Year's Day, 2 January, Good Friday, Easter Monday, Ascension, Whit Monday, Christmas Day and 26 December; and 1 May and 1 August. High holidays are Good Friday, Easter Sunday, Whit Sunday, the Federal Day of Prayer and Christmas Day. On public rest days, work, activities or events that seriously disturb the quiet of the day are banned. Shop hours follow the separate shop-hours Act (not read for this record). On high holidays, non-religious events are banned, except events in closed indoor rooms that do not have more than 500 people at once. The commune may permit an event that would otherwise be banned if it does not contradict the meaning of the high holiday, and may ban any event if there is a well-founded fear that it will disturb the day. A person who, on a high holiday, deliberately holds a non-religious event outdoors without a communal permit, holds an indoor non-religious event for more than 500 people without a permit, or holds an event the commune has banned, is fined up to CHF 10,000 (about A$17,274).
